title.zh: 卷二百〇四 列傳第九十一: 宦者
title.raw: 卷二百〇四 列傳第九十一: 宦者 Volume 204 Biographies 91: Eunuchs

sentences.zh: 前世宦者之禍嘗烈矣，元之初興，非能有鑑乎古者，然歷十有餘世，考其亂亡之所由，而初不自閹人出，何哉？

translations.literal: In previous ages the calamities of eunuchs were often severe. When the Yuan first arose, could they not take warning from antiquity? Yet passing through more than ten reigns, examining the causes of disorder and ruin, at the outset it did not arise from castrated men — why?
translations.idiomatic: In earlier dynasties, eunuchs had repeatedly brought ruin on the state. When the Yuan dynasty first rose, its founders surely knew that history — yet across more than ten reigns, if one traces the causes of chaos and collapse, at first those troubles did not spring from palace eunuchs. How was this so?

sentences.zh: 蓋自太祖選貴臣子弟給事內廷，凡飲食、冠服、書記，上所常御者，各以其職典之，而命四大功臣世為之長，號四怯薛。

translations.literal: Generally, from the time the Taizu selected sons of noble ministers to serve in the inner court, for all food, drink, headgear, robes, and clerical records that the sovereign commonly used, each was managed according to its office, and he appointed the four great meritorious officials to be heads in perpetuity, called the Four Kheshig.
translations.idiomatic: The reason lay in Taizu’s policy: he chose sons of eminent ministers to serve in the inner court. Everything the emperor routinely used — food and drink, caps and robes, written records — was kept by men assigned to those duties, while four great founding ministers and their descendants were made permanent chiefs of the establishment, known as the Four Kheshig.

sentences.zh: 故天子前後左右，皆世家大臣及其子孫之生而貴者，而宦官之擅權竊政者不得有為於其間。

translations.literal: Therefore before and behind and to the left and right of the Son of Heaven were all great ministers of hereditary families and their sons and grandsons born to nobility, and eunuchs who usurped power and stole governance could accomplish nothing among them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the men at the emperor’s side, before and behind, left and right, were scions of great ministerial houses born to rank — and eunuchs who might seize power and meddle in government had no room to act.

sentences.zh: 雖或有之，然不旋踵而遂敗。

translations.literal: Although there were sometimes such cases, yet before turning the heel they then failed.
translations.idiomatic: When such men did appear, they were crushed almost at once.

sentences.zh: 此其詒謀，可謂度越前代者矣。

translations.literal: This planning for posterity may be said to have surpassed previous ages.
translations.idiomatic: In foresight for later ages, this arrangement truly went beyond anything earlier dynasties had done.

sentences.zh: 如李邦寧者，以亡國閹豎，遭遇世祖，進齒薦紳，遂躋極品，然其言亦有可稱者焉。

translations.literal: Such as Li Bangning — as a castrated man of a perished state, encountering Shizu, advancing to rank with the gentry, then ascending to the highest grade — yet his words also had what could be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bangning, for example, was a eunuch of a fallen kingdom who won favor under Shizu, rose among the scholar-officials, and climbed to the highest ranks — yet some of what he said still deserves respect.

sentences.zh: 至於樸不花，乃東夷之人，始以西宮同里，因緣柄用，遂與權奸同惡相濟，訖底於誅戮，則固有以致之也。

translations.literal: As for Po Buhua, he was a man of the eastern Yi. At first, being from the same village as the Western Palace, by circumstance he grasped use of power, then with powerful villains aided each other’s wickedness, ending in execution and punishment — there were indeed causes that brought this about.
translations.idiomatic: Po Buhua, by contrast, came from the eastern borderlands. He had grown up in the same hometown as the empress of the Western Palace; through that connection he gained power, then joined forces with corrupt ministers until he was put to death — a fate he had largely brought on himself.

sentences.zh: 用特著之於篇。

translations.literal: Therefore they are specially set forth in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: For these reasons they are given special treatment in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗奉皇太后燕大安閣，閣中有故篋，問邦寧曰：「此何篋也？

translations.literal: The Emperor once attended the Empress Dowager at a banquet in the Great Peace Pavilion. In the pavilion was an old box. He asked Bangning: "What box is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, while hosting the empress dowager at a feast in the Great Peace Pavilion, the emperor noticed an old chest in the hall and asked Bangning, "What is this chest?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此世祖貯裘帶者。

translations.literal: " He replied: "This is where Shizu stored fur robes and belts."
translations.idiomatic: Bangning answered, "That is the chest in which Shizu kept his fur robes and belts."

sentences.zh: 臣聞有聖訓曰：'藏此以遺子孫，使見吾樸儉，可為華侈之戒。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard there was a sage instruction saying: 'Store these to bequeath to descendants, so that they may see my plainness and frugality, and it may serve as a warning against splendor and extravagance.'
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that he left a sacred instruction: 'Keep these for our descendants, so they may see how plain and frugal I was — let it warn them against luxury and excess.'

sentences.zh: '」帝命發篋視之，歎曰：「非卿言，朕安知之。

translations.literal: '" The Emperor ordered the box opened to view it, and sighed: "Had it not been for your words, how would We have known?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the chest opened and sighed. "If you had not told me, how would I ever have known?"

sentences.zh: 」時有宗王在側，遽曰：「世祖雖神聖，然嗇於財。

translations.literal: " At the time a imperial clansman was at the side and hastily said: "Shizu, though divine and sagely, was nevertheless stingy with wealth."
translations.idiomatic: A prince standing nearby blurted out, "Shizu may have been a sage, but he was miserly with money."

sentences.zh: 」邦寧曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Bangning said: "It is not so."
translations.idiomatic: Bangning replied, "That is not so."

sentences.zh: 世祖一言，無不為後世法；

translations.literal: Shizu’s every word was without exception a model for later generations;
translations.idiomatic: Every word Shizu spoke became a model for later generations;

sentences.zh: 一予奪，無不當功罪。

translations.literal: every grant or withdrawal was without exception appropriate to merit and guilt.
translations.idiomatic: every reward or punishment matched true merit and fault.

sentences.zh: 且天下所入雖富，苟用不節，必致匱乏。

translations.literal: Moreover, although the empire’s receipts were abundant, if use were not restrained, it would necessarily lead to depletion.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, however rich the empire’s income, spending without restraint would soon drain the treasury.

sentences.zh: 自先朝以來，歲賦已不足用，又數會宗籓，資費無算，旦暮不給，必將橫斂掊怨，豈美事耶。

translations.literal: From the previous reign onward, the annual levies were already insufficient for use; moreover there were repeatedly assemblies of the imperial clan, with expenses beyond reckoning. If morning and evening there were not enough, there would necessarily be harsh exactions and accumulated resentment — how could this be a fine affair?
translations.idiomatic: Since the previous reign, annual revenue has already fallen short, and repeated gatherings of the imperial clan have cost sums beyond counting. If income cannot meet daily needs, harsh levies will breed popular resentment — is that anything to admire?

sentences.zh: 」太后及帝深然其言。

translations.literal: " The Empress Dowager and the Emperor deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and the emperor were both deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 俄加大司徒、尚服院使，遙授丞相，行大司農，領太醫院事，階金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Shortly he was further appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture, Commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Office, given the title of Chancellor at a distance, acting as Grand Minister of Revenue, and overseeing the Imperial Medical Office, with rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture and made head of the Imperial Wardrobe Office, given the nominal title of chancellor while acting as Grand Minister of Revenue and supervising the Imperial Medical Office, with the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness bearing the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 太廟舊嘗遣官行事，至是復欲如之，邦寧諫曰：「先朝非不欲親致饗祀，誠以疾廢禮耳。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ancestral Temple had formerly sent officials to perform the rites; at this time they again wished to do likewise. Bangning remonstrated: "The previous reign was not unwilling to offer sacrifices in person; it was truly because illness prevented the rites."
translations.idiomatic: It had been customary to send officials to perform sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the court now wished to resume that practice. Bangning remonstrated: "The previous emperor did not refuse to sacrifice in person — he was prevented by illness."

sentences.zh: 今陛下繼成之初，正宜開彰孝道，以率先天下，躬祀太室，以成一代之典。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of Your Majesty’s succession to completion, it is just the time to open and display filial piety, to take the lead for all under Heaven, and personally sacrifice in the Grand Chamber to complete the ritual code of a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just succeeded to the throne — this is the moment to display filial devotion and set an example for the realm by sacrificing in person in the Grand Chamber, establishing the ritual standard of your reign.

sentences.zh: 循習故弊，非臣所知也。

translations.literal: Following old abuses is not what your servant understands.
translations.idiomatic: To cling to an old bad habit is not, in my view, the right course.

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 即日備法駕，宿齋宮，且命邦寧為大禮使。

translations.literal: That very day he prepared the imperial carriage according to law, lodged in the fasting palace, and moreover appointed Bangning as Grand Ritual Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he prepared the imperial procession, spent the night in the fasting palace, and appointed Bangning grand ritual commissioner.

sentences.zh: 禮成，加恩三代：曾祖頤，贈銀青光祿大夫、司徒，諡敬懿；

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, favor was extended to three generations: great-grandfather Yi was posthumously given Silver Splendid Happiness Grand Master and Minister of Education, with posthumous title Reverent and Excellent;
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, honors were extended three generations back: his great-grandfather Yi was posthumously made Silver Splendid Happiness Grand Master and Minister of Education, with the posthumous title Reverent and Excellent;

sentences.zh: 祖德懋，贈儀同三司、大司徒，諡忠獻；

translations.literal: grandfather Demao was posthumously given Equal in Protocol with the Three Excellencies and Grand Minister of Education, with posthumous title Loyal and Offering;
translations.idiomatic: his grandfather Demao was given equal protocol with the Three Excellencies and the title Grand Minister of Education, posthumously styled Loyal and Offering;

sentences.zh: 父捴，贈太保、開府儀同三司，諡文穆。

translations.literal: father Cong was posthumously given Grand Guardian, Opening the Office with Equal Protocol to the Three Excellencies, with posthumous title Cultured and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: and his father Cong was made Grand Guardian with the privilege of an office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies, posthumously titled Cultured and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，以邦寧舊臣，賜鈔千錠，辭弗受。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, because Bangning was an old minister, he was granted a thousand ingots of paper money, but he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, he granted Bangning a thousand ingots of paper money as a former servant of the house, but Bangning refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 國學將釋奠，敕遣邦寧致祭於文宣王。

translations.literal: The National Academy was about to perform the libation sacrifice; an edict dispatched Bangning to offer sacrifice to King Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the National Academy was to hold its libation ceremony for Confucius, the emperor ordered Bangning to perform the sacrifice to King Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 點視畢，至位立，殿戶方辟，忽大風起，殿上及兩廡燭盡滅，燭台底鐵鐏入地尺，無不拔者，邦寧悚息伏地，諸執事者皆伏。

translations.literal: When the inspection of the tally was finished, he came to his position and stood; the hall doors had just opened when suddenly a great wind arose. Candles in the hall and in both side corridors were all extinguished; the iron sockets at the bases of the candle stands sank a foot into the ground, and none were not uprooted. Bangning, trembling, held his breath and lay prostrate on the ground, and all those conducting the rites likewise lay prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: After the inspection was complete he took his place; the hall doors had just opened when a violent wind sprang up. Every candle in the main hall and side corridors went out, and the iron sockets of the stands were driven a foot into the floor — not one remained upright. Bangning lay trembling on the ground, and all the officiants did the same.

sentences.zh: 良久風定，乃成禮，邦寧因慚悔累日。

translations.literal: After a long while the wind settled, and only then were the rites completed. Bangning therefore felt shame and remorse for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the wind died down could the rite be completed. Bangning was ashamed and troubled for days afterward.

sentences.zh: 初，仁宗為皇太子，丞相三寶奴等用事，畏仁宗英明，邦寧揣知其意，言於武宗曰：「陛下富於春秋，皇子漸長，父作子述，古之道也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Renzong was crown prince, the chancellor Sanbaonu and others held power and feared Renzong’s brilliance. Bangning surmised their intent and spoke to Wuzong: "Your Majesty is rich in years; the prince is gradually growing. The father acts and the son carries on — this is the way of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Renzong was crown prince, Chancellor Sanbaonu and his faction held power and feared the prince’s ability. Bangning guessed their intent and said to Wuzong: "Your Majesty is still in the prime of life, and the prince is growing up. For the father to rule and the son to follow is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 未聞有子而立弟者。

translations.literal: One has not heard of having a son yet establishing a younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: One never hears of passing the throne to a younger brother while the son still lives."

sentences.zh: 」武宗不悅曰：「朕志已定，汝自往東宮言之。

translations.literal: " Wuzong, displeased, said: "Our resolve is already fixed. You yourself go to the Eastern Palace and speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was displeased. "My mind is made up. Go tell the Eastern Palace yourself."

sentences.zh: 」邦寧慚懼而退。

translations.literal: " Bangning, ashamed and afraid, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Bangning withdrew in shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，左右咸請誅之，仁宗曰：「帝王歷數，自有天命，其言何足介懷。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, those at his left and right all requested that Bangning be executed. Renzong said: "The imperial succession has its own mandate of Heaven; how are his words worth taking to heart?"
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong succeeded, his attendants all urged that Bangning be put to death. Renzong said, "The imperial succession rests on Heaven’s mandate — why should I trouble myself over what he said?"

sentences.zh: 」加邦寧開府儀同三司，為集賢院大學士。

translations.literal: " He further appointed Bangning Opening the Office with Equal Protocol to the Three Excellencies and made him Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he promoted Bangning to the privilege of an office equal in protocol to the Three Excellencies and made him grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 樸不花，高麗人，亦曰王不花。

translations.literal: Po Buhua was a man of Goryeo; he was also called Wang Buhua.
translations.idiomatic: Po Buhua — also known as Wang Buhua — was from Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 皇后奇氏微時，與不花同鄉里，相為依倚。

translations.literal: When Empress Qi was in humble circumstances, she and Buhua were from the same village and relied on each other.
translations.idiomatic: In her early days Empress Qi came from the same hometown as Buhua, and the two relied on each other.

sentences.zh: 及選為宮人，有寵，遂為第二皇后，居興聖宮，生皇太子愛猷識理達臘。

translations.literal: When she was selected as a palace woman and gained favor, she then became the second empress, residing in the Palace of Sagely Origin, and bore the crown prince Ayurshiridara.
translations.idiomatic: After she entered the palace and won favor, she became second empress, lived in the Palace of Sagely Origin, and bore the crown prince Ayurshiridara.

sentences.zh: 於是不花以閹人入事皇后者有年，皇后愛幸之，情意甚膠固，累遷官至榮祿大夫、資正院使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Buhua, as a eunuch, entered to serve the empress for many years. The empress favored and cherished him; their feelings were very firmly glued. By repeated promotions he reached the offices of Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and Commissioner of the Rectification of Resources Office.
translations.idiomatic: Buhua had then served the empress for years as a eunuch. She favored him deeply, and their bond was very close. Through repeated promotions he rose to Grand Master for Glorious Happiness and commissioner of the Rectification of Resources Office.

sentences.zh: 資正院者，皇后之財賦悉隸焉。

translations.literal: The Rectification of Resources Office was where all the empress’s wealth and levies were subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: That office controlled all of the empress’s revenues and property.

sentences.zh: 至正十八年，京師大饑​​疫，時河南北、山東郡縣皆被兵，民之老幼男女，避居聚京師，以故死者相枕藉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, the capital suffered great famine and pestilence. At that time the commanderies and counties north and south of the Yellow River in Henan and Shandong were all afflicted by warfare. Old and young, male and female among the people, fleeing to dwell, gathered in the capital; for this reason the dead lay pillow upon pillow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhizheng, famine and plague struck the capital. Fighting had ravaged counties across Henan, north of the Yellow River, and Shandong, and refugees of every age and sex crowded into Dadu until the dead lay stacked upon one another.

sentences.zh: 不花欲要譽一時，請於帝，市地收瘞之，帝賜鈔七千錠，中宮及興聖、隆福兩宮，皇太子、皇太子妃，賜金銀及他物有差，省院施者無算；

translations.literal: Buhua wished to win reputation for a time and requested of the Emperor to purchase land to gather and bury them. The Emperor granted seven thousand ingots of paper money; the Central Palace and the two palaces of Sagely Origin and Longevity and Blessings, the crown prince and the crown prince’s consort, granted gold, silver, and other goods in varying amounts; the provincial and central offices gave without reckoning;
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a moment’s fame, Buhua asked the emperor to buy land for mass burial. The emperor gave seven thousand ingots of paper money; the central palace, the palaces of Sagely Origin and Longevity and Blessings, the crown prince and his consort each contributed gold, silver, and other goods in varying amounts; and the central and provincial offices gave without limit.

sentences.zh: 不花出玉帶一、金帶一、銀二錠、米三十四斛、麥六斛、青貂銀鼠裘各一襲以為費。

translations.literal: Buhua himself contributed one jade belt, one gold belt, two ingots of silver, thirty-four hu of rice, six hu of wheat, and one set each of blue sable and silver-rat fur garments as expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Buhua himself supplied one jade belt, one gold belt, two ingots of silver, thirty-four hu of rice, six hu of wheat, and one blue-sable and one silver-rat fur robe as his share of the cost.

sentences.zh: 擇地自南北兩城​​抵盧溝橋，掘深及泉，男女異壙，人以一屍至者，隨給以鈔，舁負相踵。

translations.literal: They selected land from the southern and northern two cities as far as the Lugou Bridge, dug deep to reach spring water, and made separate burial mounds for men and women. For each person who brought one corpse, paper money was given on the spot; bearers followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Land was chosen from the southern and northern quarters of the city to the Lugou Bridge. Graves were dug down to the water table, with separate plots for men and women. Anyone who brought a corpse was paid in paper money on the spot, and bearers came in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 既覆土，就萬安壽慶寺建無遮大會。

translations.literal: After the earth was covered, at the Ten Thousand Peace Longevity Celebration Temple they established a universal assembly.
translations.idiomatic: After the burials, a universal Buddhist assembly was held at the Ten Thousand Peace Longevity Celebration Temple.

sentences.zh: 至二十年四月，前後瘞者二十萬，用鈔二萬七千九十餘錠、米五百六十餘石。

translations.literal: By the fourth month of the twentieth year, those buried before and after numbered two hundred thousand; paper money used was more than twenty-seven thousand and ninety ingots, and rice more than five hundred and sixty shi.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month of the twentieth year, two hundred thousand bodies had been interred, at a cost of more than twenty-seven thousand ingots of paper money and more than five hundred and sixty shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 又於大悲寺修水陸大會三晝夜，凡居民病者予之藥，不能喪者給之棺。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the Great Compassion Temple they conducted a water-and-land great assembly for three days and nights. All residents who were ill were given medicine; those unable to perform funerals were given coffins.
translations.idiomatic: He also held a three-day water-and-land Buddhist ceremony at the Great Compassion Temple, distributed medicine to the sick, and gave coffins to those who could not afford burial.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨張翥為文頌其事，曰《善惠之碑》。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician and Court Drafter Zhang Zhu composed a text praising the affair, called "The Stele of Good Grace" (Shanhui zhi bei).
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Zhang Zhu wrote a commemorative text titled "The Stele of Good Grace" (Shanhui zhi bei).

sentences.zh: 於是帝在位久，而皇太子春秋日盛，軍國之事，皆其所臨決。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor had long been on the throne, while the crown prince’s years daily flourished; military and state affairs were all decided under his oversight.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had reigned many years, while the crown prince was coming of age and already decided most military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇后乃謀內禪皇太子，而使不花喻意於丞相太平，太平不答。

translations.literal: The empress then plotted to abdicate the throne internally to the crown prince and had Buhua convey her intent to Chancellor Taiping; Taiping did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The empress then plotted to abdicate in favor of the crown prince and sent Buhua to sound out Chancellor Taiping, who gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 二十年，太平乃罷去，而獨搠思監為丞相。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Taiping was finally dismissed and left office, and Bodashirin alone became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Taiping was finally removed, leaving Bodashirin as sole chancellor.

sentences.zh: 時帝益厭政，不花乘間用事，與搠思監相為表裡，四方警報、將臣功狀，皆抑而不聞，內外解體。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor increasingly grew weary of government. Buhua seized the interval to wield power, and with Bodashirin acted as outer and inner to each other. Alarms from the four directions and the merit-records of generals and ministers were all suppressed and not heard; within and without, the structure dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew ever more weary of governing. Buhua seized the chance to rule through him, working hand in glove with Bodashirin. Reports of danger from every quarter and accounts of generals’ achievements were suppressed, and the government fell apart inside and out.

sentences.zh: 然根株盤固，氣焰薰灼，內外百官趨附之者十九。

translations.literal: Yet their roots and stems were firmly coiled, their aura blazing hot; of officials within and without who rushed to attach themselves, there were nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their power was deeply rooted and their arrogance blazed; nine officials in ten, inside and outside the court, flocked to their side.

sentences.zh: 又宣政院使脫歡，與之同惡相濟，為國大蠹。

translations.literal: Moreover, Commissioner of the Bureau for the Propagation of Governance Tohuan aided their wickedness together with them, becoming a great borer in the state.
translations.idiomatic: Tohuan, commissioner of the Bureau for the Propagation of Governance, joined their conspiracy and became a great plague on the realm.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，監察御史也先帖木兒、孟也先不花、傅公讓等乃劾奏樸不花、脫歡奸邪，當屏黜。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Investigating Censor Yesian Timur, Meng Yesian Buhua, Fu Gongrang, and others then memorialized impeaching Po Buhua and Tohuan for wickedness and treachery, saying they should be removed and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, investigating censors Yesian Timur, Meng Yesian Buhua, Fu Gongrang, and others memorialized the throne, charging Po Buhua and Tohuan with corruption and demanding their removal.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫老的沙以其事聞，皇太子執不下，而皇后庇之尤固，御史乃皆坐左遷。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Laodasha reported the matter to the throne. The crown prince held the memorial and would not release it, while the empress sheltered them all the more firmly. The censors therefore all suffered demotion to lesser posts.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Laodasha reported the matter, but the crown prince withheld the memorial. The empress shielded the accused all the more stubbornly, and every censor involved was demoted.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史陳祖仁，連上皇太子書切諫之，而台臣大小皆辭職，皇太子乃為言於帝，令二人皆辭退。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Censor Chen Zuren repeatedly submitted letters to the crown prince with stern remonstrance. The censorial officials great and small all resigned their posts. The crown prince then spoke on their behalf to the Emperor and ordered the two men to resign and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary censor Chen Zuren sent the crown prince letter after letter of sharp remonstrance. Censors great and small resigned en masse, and the crown prince finally persuaded the emperor to have both men step down.

sentences.zh: 而祖仁言猶不已，又上皇帝書言：「二人亂階禍本，今不芟除，後必不利。

translations.literal: Yet Zuren’s words still did not cease. He again submitted a letter to the Emperor saying: "These two men are the root of disorder and the source of calamity. If they are not cut down and removed now, later there will necessarily be harm."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zuren would not be silenced. He wrote again to the emperor: "These two are the root of disorder. If they are not cut down now, disaster will follow.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐季世，其禍皆起此輩，而權臣、籓鎮乘之。

translations.literal: In the late ages of Han and Tang, their calamities all arose from this sort; then powerful ministers and frontier commanders seized the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Han and Tang dynasties, ruin began with men like these, and powerful ministers and regional warlords took advantage.

sentences.zh: 故千尋之木，吞舟之魚，其腐敗必由於內，陛下誠思之，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Therefore a tree of a thousand fathoms, a fish that swallows boats — their decay and ruin must proceed from within. Your Majesty, if you truly reflect on this, it may make one’s heart turn cold.
translations.idiomatic: A tree a thousand fathoms tall and a fish that can swallow a boat rot from within — Your Majesty should ponder this; it is enough to chill the heart.

sentences.zh: 臣願俯從臺諫之言，將二人特加擯斥，不令以辭退為名，成其奸計。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty will bow to follow the censorial remonstrance, specially add rejection and expulsion of the two men, and not let them take the name of resignation, completing their treacherous scheme.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed the censors and explicitly expel these two men — not let them resign on their own terms and thus complete their scheme."

sentences.zh: 海內皆知陛下信賞必罰，自此二人始，將士孰不效力，寇賊亦皆喪膽，天下可全，而有以還祖宗之舊。

translations.literal: All within the seas will know that Your Majesty’s trust in rewards and certain punishments begins with these two men. Which soldier and officer would not exert his strength? Bandits and rebels would also all lose their gall. The realm could be preserved, and there would be means to restore the old ways of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: If the realm sees that Your Majesty rewards the loyal and punishes the wicked, beginning with these two, which soldier will not fight his hardest? Rebels will lose heart, the empire can be saved, and the house can be restored to its former glory.

sentences.zh: 若優柔不斷，彼惡日盈，將不可製。

translations.literal: If you are irresolute and cannot decide, their wickedness will daily increase and will become impossible to control.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty hesitates, their evil will grow daily until it can no longer be checked.

sentences.zh: 臣寧餓死於家，誓不與同朝，牽聯及禍。

translations.literal: Your servant would rather starve to death at home, swearing not to serve in the same court with them, lest being drawn along bring calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather starve at home than serve in the same court with them and be swept into their ruin."

sentences.zh: 」語具《陳祖仁傳》。

translations.literal: " The words are given in full in the biography of Chen Zuren (Chen Zuren zhuan).
translations.idiomatic: The full text appears in the biography of Chen Zuren (Chen Zuren zhuan).

sentences.zh: 會侍御史李國鳳亦上書皇太子，言：「不花驕恣無上，招權納賂，奔競之徒，皆出其門，駸駸有趙高、張讓、田令孜之風，漸不可長，眾人所共知之，獨主上與殿下未之知耳。

translations.literal: At the same time Attending Censor Li Guofeng also submitted a letter to the crown prince, saying: "Buhua is arrogant and unrestrained above all, gathers power and receives bribes; those who rush to compete all come from his gate. Gradually he has the manner of Zhao Gao, Zhang Rang, and Tian Lingzi — this cannot be allowed to grow. What the multitude jointly knows, only the sovereign and Your Highness do not yet know."
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, attending censor Li Guofeng wrote to the crown prince: "Buhua is insolent beyond measure, sells offices and takes bribes, and every schemer in the capital passes through his door. He increasingly resembles Zhao Gao, Zhang Rang, and Tian Lingzi. Everyone knows this — only Your Majesty and Your Highness seem not to."

sentences.zh: 自古宦者，近君親上，使少得志，未有不為國家禍者。

translations.literal: From antiquity, eunuchs who drew near the ruler and were intimate with their superiors, if allowed to gain their wishes while young, have never failed to become calamities to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, eunuchs who win the ruler’s ear while still young have never failed to bring disaster on the state.

sentences.zh: 望殿下思履霜堅冰之戒，早賜奏聞，投之西夷，以快眾心，則紀綱可振。

translations.literal: I hope Your Highness will reflect on the warning of treading frost and solid ice, early grant memorial and report, cast him to the western barbarians to satisfy the multitude’s hearts — then the statutes and discipline can be revived.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Highness to remember the proverb about frost underfoot and ice ahead — report to the emperor at once, banish him to the western marches to satisfy public outrage, and the laws can be restored.

sentences.zh: 紀綱振，則天下之公論為可畏，法度為不可犯，政治修而百廢舉矣。

translations.literal: When statutes and discipline are revived, then the public opinion of all under Heaven becomes something to be feared and law and regulation become what cannot be violated; government is repaired and a hundred neglected affairs are raised up.
translations.idiomatic: When discipline is restored, public opinion will again command respect, the law will again be inviolable, government will function, and every neglected task can be taken up again."

sentences.zh: 」由是帝大怒，國鳳、祖仁等亦皆左遷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Emperor was greatly enraged, and Guofeng, Zuren, and the others were also all demoted to lesser posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, and Li Guofeng, Chen Zuren, and the others were all demoted.

sentences.zh: 時老的沙執其事頗力，皇太子因惡之，而皇后又譖之於內，帝以老的沙母舅故，封為雍王，遣歸國。

translations.literal: At that time Laodasha had pursued the matter with considerable force. The crown prince therefore hated him, while the empress also slandered him within. Because Laodasha was the Emperor’s maternal uncle, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong and sent back to his domain.
translations.idiomatic: Laodasha had pressed the case vigorously, and the crown prince came to dislike him. The empress slandered him within the palace, but because he was the emperor’s uncle on the mother’s side, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong and sent home.

sentences.zh: 已而復以不花為集賢大學士、崇正院使，皇后之力也。

translations.literal: Before long Buhua was again made Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents and Commissioner of the Office for the Veneration of Rectitude — through the empress’s power.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, however, Buhua was reappointed grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents and commissioner of the Office for the Veneration of Rectitude — thanks to the empress’s influence.

sentences.zh: 老的沙至大同，遂留孛羅帖木兒軍中。

translations.literal: Laodasha reached Datong and then remained in Boluo Timur’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Laodasha reached Datong and stayed with Boluo Timur’s army.

sentences.zh: 是時，搠思監、樸不花方倚擴廓帖木兒為外援，怨孛羅帖木兒匿老的沙不遣，遂誣孛羅帖木兒與老的沙謀不軌。

translations.literal: At this time Bodashirin and Po Buhua were just then relying on Köke Temür as external support. They resented Boluo Timur for harboring Laodasha and not sending him back, and therefore slandered Boluo Timur and Laodasha as plotting treason.
translations.idiomatic: Bodashirin and Po Buhua were then counting on Köke Temür as their outside ally. Angry that Boluo Timur was sheltering Laodasha, they accused Boluo Timur and Laodasha of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，詔削其官，使解兵柄歸四川。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year an edict stripped his offices and ordered him to relinquish military authority and return to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year an edict stripped Boluo Timur of his offices and ordered him to lay down command and return to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒知不出帝意，皆搠思監、樸不花所為，怒不奉詔。

translations.literal: Boluo Timur knew this did not come from the Emperor’s own intent but was all done by Bodashirin and Po Buhua. In anger he did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo Timur knew the order did not reflect the emperor’s true will but came from Bodashirin and Po Buhua, and he refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 宗王不顏帖木兒等為表言其誣枉，而朝廷亦畏其強不可製，復下詔數搠思監、樸不花互相壅蔽簧惑主聽之罪，屏搠思監於嶺北，竄樸不花於甘肅，以快眾憤，而復孛羅帖木兒官爵。

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Buyan Timur and others submitted a memorial stating he had been falsely accused. The court also feared his strength and that he could not be controlled. They again issued an edict enumerating the crimes of Bodashirin and Po Buhua in mutually obstructing and deceiving the sovereign’s hearing, banished Bodashirin to the region north of the ranges, and exiled Po Buhua to Gansu to satisfy popular anger, while restoring Boluo Timur’s offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Buyan Timur and others memorialized that Boluo Timur had been framed. The court also feared his power. A new edict listed Bodashirin’s and Po Buhua’s crimes of blocking the emperor’s ears and deceiving him, banished Bodashirin to the northern frontier, exiled Po Buhua to Gansu to appease public anger, and restored Boluo Timur’s rank.

sentences.zh: 然搠思監、樸不花皆留京城，實未嘗行。

translations.literal: Yet Bodashirin and Po Buhua both remained in the capital and in truth had never departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bodashirin and Po Buhua both stayed in the capital and never actually left.

sentences.zh: 未幾，孛羅帖木兒遣禿堅帖木兒以兵向闕，聲言清君側之惡。

translations.literal: Before long Boluo Timur dispatched Tujian Timur with troops toward the palace, proclaiming that he would clear the wicked from the ruler’s side.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Boluo Timur sent Tujian Timur with an army toward the capital, claiming he would purge evil from the ruler’s side.

sentences.zh: 四月十二日，駐於清河，帝遣達達國師問故，往復者數四，言必得搠思監、樸不花乃退兵。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the fourth month he encamped at Qinghe. The Emperor sent the Dada National Preceptor to inquire the cause; they went back and forth several times. He said he must obtain Bodashirin and Po Buhua before he would withdraw his troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day of the fourth month his force halted at Qinghe. The emperor sent the Dada National Preceptor to ask his purpose; after several exchanges Boluo Timur said he would withdraw only if Bodashirin and Po Buhua were handed over.

sentences.zh: 帝度其勢不可解，不得已，執兩人畀之，其兵乃退。

translations.literal: The Emperor judged that the situation could not be resolved and, having no alternative, seized the two men and handed them over; only then did his troops withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no other way out, the emperor had the two men seized and delivered to him, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 樸不花遂為孛羅帖木兒所殺。

translations.literal: Po Buhua was then killed by Boluo Timur.
translations.idiomatic: Po Buhua was killed by Boluo Timur.

sentences.zh: 事具搠思監、孛羅帖木兒傳。

translations.literal: The affair is given in full in the biographies of Bodashirin and Boluo Timur.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biographies of Bodashirin and Boluo Timur.
